headlinePool.title: Powerful storms in US midwest leave three dead and 800,000 without power
headlinePool.description: Winds of more than 80mph, severe flooding and tornadoes swept through Indiana, Ohio, Illinois and Kentucky Powerful storms swept across ⁠the midwest on Tuesday, leaving three dead and more than 800,000 without power in four states as winds gusts of more than 80mph (130km/h) tore down trees and power lines. ⁠In Indiana , a four-year-old child died after a tree fell on his ⁠home in Geneva Township and a person died in a suspected weather-related house explosion in Portage, a city about 30 miles south-east of Chicago.

headlinePool.title: Police link Welsh valleys death to biker gang rivalry
headlinePool.description: Investigators believe Vikings and Hells Angels members involved in violence that preceded death of Brecon man A man was killed in what is believed to have been a violent brawl between rival motorcycle gangs in the south Wales valleys, police have said. Anthony “Tony” Jones, 56, of Brecon, died of his injuries in hospital after the violence in Pontnewynydd, near Pontypool, last Thursday evening, which reportedly involved knives and hammers.

headlinePool.title: His wedding guests gave $6k to fund a health startup. Now it's won a $3 million prize
headlinePool.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi founded Last Mile Health to bring healthcare to people living in remote areas. The group is the 2026 recipient of the Conrad N. Hilton Humanitarian Prize.

headlinePool.title: Massive bailout for Australia’s largest aluminium smelter to be announced by PM and NSW premier
headlinePool.description: Rio Tinto said in December it may cease operations at the Tomago aluminium smelter at the end of its current electricity supply contract Resources giant Rio Tinto said in December it was contemplating ceasing operations at the Tomago aluminium smelter, located north-west of Newcastle, at the end of its current electricity supply contract.

headlinePool.title: Bridget Phillipson condemns Richard Tice’s ‘chilling attempt to silence free press’
headlinePool.description: Labour chair says Reform deputy leader is trying to harass journalists over reporting on his financial affairs UK politics live – latest updates Richard Tice has been accused by Labour’s Bridget Phillipson of mounting a “deeply chilling attempt to silence the free press” after he sent a legal threat to the Guardian over its reporting on his financial affairs. Lawyers for Tice, the deputy leader of Reform UK, singled out a Guardian correspondent for her journalism about a series of Tice’s financial transactions that were referred to the National Crime Agency.

headlinePool.title: Zhu Rongji, who drove China's 1990s economic reforms, has died at 97
headlinePool.description: Zhu was renowned for reforms that sought to transition China from the post-Maoist years to a more global market-oriented financial system, without ceding party control over the economy.

headlinePool.description: In a recent study, evolution gets even messier than usual.
